description: [Industry Code C] - The Industry Classification Codes of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (2012 Edition).
[Longitude of the Registered Address] - The longitude of the company's registered address.
[Latitude of the Registered Address] - The latitude of the company's registered address.

[Monetary Funds] - The total amount of a company's cash on hand, bank settlement account deposits, out-of-town deposits, bank draft deposits, bank cashier's check deposits, credit card deposits, and letter of credit margin deposits. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Among them: Customer Funds Deposits] - The amount of customer funds deposits of financial enterprises.

[Settlement Reserve Funds] - Funds deposited by financial enterprises engaged in securities business into designated clearing agencies for the purpose of fund clearing and settlement of securities transactions.
[Among them: Customer Reserve Funds] - Customer reserve funds obtained from securities brokerage business.
[Cash and Deposits with the Central Bank] - The total amount of cash held by the enterprise and deposits with the central bank.
[Deposits with Other Financial Institutions] - Funds deposited by the enterprise (bank) in domestic and foreign banks and non-bank financial institutions.
[Precious Metals] - The cost of gold, silver, and other precious metal inventories held by the enterprise (financial institution).

[Net Funds Lent] - Net funds lent is the difference between the funds lent by the enterprise (financial institution) to other domestic and foreign financial institutions and the related loan loss provision accounts.

[Trading Financial Assets] - Trading financial assets refer to the fair value of bond investments, stock investments, fund investments, and other trading financial assets held by the enterprise for trading purposes. Financial assets that the enterprise directly designates to be measured at fair value with changes in fair value recognized in profit or loss for the current period are also accounted for under this item. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Derivative Financial Assets] - The amount of derivative instruments, hedging instruments, and hedged items that are classified as derivative financial assets held by the enterprise.

[Net Short-Term Investments] - The difference between "Short-Term Investments" and "Provision for Short-Term Investment Decline in Value". Short-term investments are various investments purchased by the company that can be readily realized and are intended to be realized at any time, including stocks and bonds held for no more than one year (inclusive), as well as other investments with a holding period of no more than one year (inclusive). This item has been in use since 1998. Although it was discontinued in 2007 under the new accounting standards, it is retained in this database.

[Net Notes Receivable] - It is the difference between "Notes Receivable" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Notes receivable are the notes received by the company that have not yet matured and have not been discounted with a bank, including commercial acceptance bills and bank acceptance bills. However, it does not include endorsed and transferred notes receivable. This item has been in use since 1991.

[Net Accounts Receivable] - It is the difference between "Accounts Receivable" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Accounts receivable are amounts that the company should collect from the purchasing unit or the unit receiving services due to business such as selling goods, products, materials, providing services, and handling project settlements. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Receivables Financing] - An enterprise sells its accounts receivable to a bank or other financial institutions, but the bank or other financial institutions have the right of recourse. That is, if the accounts receivable cannot be collected, the bank or other financial institutions have the right to demand payment from the enterprise. This item has been in use since 2019.

[Net Prepayments] - It is the difference between the sum of the debit balances of "Advance Payments" and "Accounts Payable" minus the "Allowance for Bad Debts". Prepayments are amounts paid in advance by the enterprise to the supplier according to the purchase contract.

[Net Premiums Receivable] - It is the difference between "Premiums Receivable" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Premiums receivable are the insurance premiums that financial enterprises should collect from policyholders but have not yet received.

[Net Reinsurance Receivables] - It is the difference between "Reinsurance Receivables" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Reinsurance receivables are amounts that the enterprise (insurance company) should collect from engaging in reinsurance business.

[Net Subrogation Receivables] - It is the difference between "Subrogation Receivables" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Subrogation receivables refer to the compensation that the insurer is entitled to claim from the third-party liable person after assuming the insurance liability and legally obtaining the right of subrogation from the insured.

[Net Reinsurance Contract Reserves Receivable] - It is the difference between "Reinsurance Contract Reserves Receivable" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Reinsurance contract reserves receivable are the unearned premium reserves and insurance liability reserves that the enterprise (ceding reinsurer) recognizes as receivable from engaging in reinsurance business and should be recovered from the reinsurance acceptor. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Among them: Net Unearned Premium Reserves Receivable from Reinsurance] - It belongs to the ceded unearned premiums and is an adjustment to the current period's ceded premiums.

[Among them: Net Outstanding Claims Reserves Receivable from Reinsurance] - It is the difference between "Outstanding Claims Reserves Receivable from Reinsurance" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Outstanding claims reserves receivable from reinsurance are the reserves for outstanding claims that the enterprise should recover from the reinsurance acceptor, net of the accumulated impairment provisions, recognized in the course of reinsurance business.

[Among them: Net Life Insurance Reserves Receivable from Reinsurance] - It is the difference between "Life Insurance Reserves Receivable from Reinsurance" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Life insurance reserves receivable from reinsurance are the life insurance reserves that the enterprise should recover from the reinsurance acceptor, net of the accumulated impairment provisions, recognized in the course of reinsurance business.

[Among them: Net Long-Term Health Insurance Reserves Receivable from Reinsurance] - It is the difference between "Long-Term Health Insurance Reserves Receivable from Reinsurance" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Long-term health insurance reserves receivable from reinsurance are the long-term health insurance reserves that the enterprise should recover from the reinsurance acceptor, net of the accumulated impairment provisions, recognized in the course of reinsurance business.

[Net Interest Receivable] - It is the difference between "Interest Receivable" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Interest receivable refers to the interest that the company should receive from debt investments. The interest receivable from bonds purchased with principal and interest repaid at maturity is not included in this item. This item has been in use since 1998.

[Net Dividends Receivable] - It is the difference between "Dividends Receivable" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Dividends receivable are the cash dividends that the company should receive from equity investments. The profits receivable from other units by the company are also included in this item. This item has been in use since 1998.

[Net Other Receivables] - It is the difference between "Other Receivables" and "Allowance for Bad Debts of Other Receivables". Other receivables are various receivables and temporary payments of the enterprise, excluding margin deposits, financial assets purchased under resale agreements, notes receivable, accounts receivable, prepayments, dividends receivable, interest receivable, subrogation receivables, reinsurance receivables, reinsurance contract reserves receivable, long-term receivables, etc. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Financial Assets Purchased under Resale Agreements] - It is the difference between "Financial Assets Purchased under Resale Agreements" and "Allowance for Bad Debts". Financial assets purchased under resale agreements are the funds provided by the enterprise (financial institution) to purchase bills, securities, loans, etc. under an agreement to resell them at a fixed price. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Inventory] - It is the difference between "Inventory" and "Provision for Inventory Decline in Value". Inventory refers to the finished goods or merchandise held for sale in the ordinary course of business, work in progress, and materials or supplies consumed in the production process or in providing services. This item has been in use since 1990.

[Contract Assets] - It refers to the enterprise's right to receive consideration for the goods transferred to the customer, and this right depends on factors other than the passage of time. For example, if an enterprise sells two clearly distinguishable goods to a customer and is entitled to receive payment for one of the goods already delivered, but the receipt of this payment also depends on the delivery of the other good, the enterprise should classify this right to receive payment as contract assets. The enterprise's unconditional right (i.e., depending only on the passage of time) to receive consideration from the customer should be separately presented as accounts receivable. This item has been in use since 2018.
[Non-Current Assets Due within One Year] - The book value of non-current assets that are due within one year held by the company. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Margin Deposits] - Various margin deposits made or paid by the enterprise (financial institution) due to business requirements.
[Other Current Assets] - Current assets that cannot be included in other current asset items. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Total Current Assets] - The sum of all current asset items. Financial enterprises do not calculate this item. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Net Policyholder Pledged Loans] - It is the difference between "Policyholder Pledged Loans" and the related loan loss provision accounts.
[Time Deposits] - It refers to the time deposits placed by insurance companies in financial institutions.
[Net Loans and Advances] - The amount of loans and discounted assets issued by the enterprise, net of the ending balance of loan loss provisions.

[Debt Investments] - Debt investments generally refer to bond investments. Bond investment is an investment approach where bond purchasers (investors, creditors) invest capital by buying bonds, and upon maturity, they receive fixed interest and reclaim the principal from the bond issuers (borrowers, debtors). The main investors in bonds include insurance companies, commercial banks, investment firms or investment banks, and various fund organizations. This item has been in use since 2019.

[Net Available-for-Sale Financial Assets] - Net available-for-sale financial assets are the difference between the available-for-sale financial assets and the net impairment provisions for available-for-sale financial assets. Available-for-sale financial assets are the fair value of financial assets that an enterprise holds and classifies as available for sale, including equity investments and bond investments categorized as such. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Other Debt Investments] - The company makes debt investments other than bonds, such as entrusted loans with a term exceeding one year (excluding one year). This item has been in use since 2019.

[Net Held-to-Maturity Investments] - Net held-to-maturity investments are the difference between held-to-maturity investments and the impairment provisions for held-to-maturity investments. Held-to-maturity investments refer to non-derivative financial assets with a fixed maturity date, fixed or determinable recovery amounts, and where the enterprise has a clear intention and ability to hold them until maturity. Generally, treasury bonds, corporate bonds, financial bonds, etc., that an enterprise holds and that have publicly quoted prices in active markets can be classified as held-to-maturity investments. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Long-Term Receivables] - Net long-term receivables are the difference among long-term receivables, the allowance for bad debts, and unrealized financing income. Long-term receivables are the enterprise's long-term receivable amounts, including receivables arising from finance leases, sales of goods and provision of services with financing nature on a deferred basis, etc. Long-term equity that essentially constitutes a net investment in the invested entity is also accounted for under this item. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Long-Term Equity Investments] - Net long-term equity investments are the difference between long-term equity investments and the impairment provisions for long-term equity investments. Since 2007, this item has been in use. Before 2007, long-term equity investments were defined as various equity investments that the company did not intend to liquidate within one year (including one year), including purchased stocks and other equity investments. After the new accounting standards in 2007, the original "long-term equity investments" were respectively accounted for in "long-term equity investments", "available-for-sale financial assets", and "goodwill".

[Investments in Other Equity Instruments] - This item is used to account for non-trading equity instrument investments designated by the enterprise to be measured at fair value with changes in fair value recognized in other comprehensive income. This item can be accounted for in detail according to the categories and types of other equity instrument investments, including "cost", "interest adjustment", and "changes in fair value". This item has been in use since 2018.
[Other Non-Current Financial Assets] - Other non-current financial assets. This item has been in use since 2019.

[Net Long-Term Debt Investments] - Net long-term debt investments are the difference between long-term debt investments and the impairment provisions for long-term debt investments. These include various debt investments, such as bond investments, that the company does not plan to liquidate within one year (including one year). Although the item of long-term debt investments was cancelled after the new accounting standards in 2007, it is retained in this database.

[Net Long-Term Investments] - Net long-term investments are the difference between the total of all long-term investment items and the impairment provisions for long-term investments. Long-term investment items include long-term equity investments, long-term bond investments, and other long-term investments. This item has been in use since 1998. Although it was discontinued under the new accounting standards in 2007, it is retained in this database.
[Capital Margin Deposits] - Capital margin deposits paid by enterprises (insurance companies) in accordance with the specified proportion.

[Separate Account Assets] - The value of separate account assets recognized by enterprises (insurance companies) for the portion of investment-linked products that is not part of the risk protection and is accounted for separately.

[Net Investment Property] - Investment property refers to real estate held for the purpose of earning rental income or capital appreciation, or both, including leased land use rights, land use rights held for transfer after appreciation, and leased buildings. Net investment property is the difference between investment property, the impairment provisions for investment property, and the accumulated depreciation of investment property. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Fixed Assets] - Net fixed assets are the amount remaining after deducting accumulated depreciation and impairment provisions for fixed assets from the original cost of fixed assets. Fixed assets include the original cost of fixed assets held by the enterprise, the temporary facilities of construction contractors, and the software accompanying the purchase of computer hardware that is not priced separately, which are also accounted for under this item. Since 2000, this item has been in use. After the new accounting standards in 2007, fixed assets that meet the definition of "investment property" are accounted for under the "Investment Property" item.

[Net Construction in Progress] - The difference between "Construction in Progress" and the impairment provisions for construction in progress. Construction in Progress represents the actual expenditures of the company on various unfinished projects at the end of the period, including the land price for occupied land, preliminary preparation expenses, the value of equipment delivered for installation, materials consumed in unfinished construction and installation projects, basic construction management fees, the advance payment for outsourced projects, and the costs of construction and installation projects that have been completed but not yet put into use. This item has been in use since 2000.
[Project Materials] - The actual cost of project materials that have not been used in various projects of the company. This item has been in use since 1997.

[Fixed Assets Disposal] - The net value of fixed assets that the company has transferred for disposal due to reasons such as sale, damage, or scrapping but have not yet been completely disposed of, as well as the difference between the disposal expenses and the proceeds from the disposal of these fixed assets during the disposal process. This item has been in use since 1992.

[Net Productive Biological Assets] - Net productive biological assets are the difference between productive biological assets and the impairment provisions for productive biological assets. Productive biological assets refer to biological assets held for the purpose of producing agricultural products, providing labor services, or leasing, including economic forests, fuelwood forests, productive livestock, and draft animals. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Oil and Gas Assets] - Net oil and gas assets are the difference between oil and gas assets and accumulated depletion. Oil and gas assets are the original cost of mining rights, oil and gas wells, and related facilities held by enterprises (engaged in oil and gas extraction).
[Right-of-Use Assets] - The right of the lessee to use the leased assets during the lease term. This item has been in use since 2019.

[Net Intangible Assets] - Net intangible assets are the amount remaining after deducting amortization and impairment provisions from the original cost of various intangible assets of the company. The company's intangible assets include patent rights, non-patented technologies, trademark rights, copyrights, and land use rights. This item has been in use since 2000. After the new accounting standards in 2007, the original intangible assets are accounted for separately under "Intangible Assets," "Goodwill," and "Investment Property".
[Among them: Recoverable Amount of Trading Seat Fees] - The recoverable amount of trading seat fees paid by securities companies.
[Development Expenditures] - The portion that has been capitalized during the development process but has not yet been converted into intangible assets. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Goodwill] - Net goodwill is the difference between goodwill and the impairment provisions for goodwill. Goodwill is the value of goodwill formed in business combinations. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Long-Term Deferred Expenses] - Various expenses of the company that have not yet been amortized, with an amortization period of more than one year (excluding one year) excluding organization expenses, such as expenditures on the improvement of leased fixed assets, major repair expenditures, and other deferred expenses with an amortization period of more than one year (excluding one year). This item has been in use since 1998.
[Deferred Tax Assets] - Deferred tax assets recognized by the enterprise arising from deductible temporary differences. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Agency Business Assets] - Mainly used to account for the assets formed from agency business where the enterprise does not assume risks, including securities investments and entrusted loans carried out through entrusted wealth management business.
[Other Non-Current Assets] - The total of non-current assets of the enterprise other than the above-mentioned non-current assets. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Total Non-Current Assets] - The total of the above-mentioned non-current assets. Financial enterprises do not calculate this item. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Other Assets] - Other assets disclosed by financial enterprises.
[Total Assets] - The total of all asset items. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Short-Term Borrowings] - Borrowings by the company that have not yet been repaid and have a term of one year or less (including one year).
[Among them: Pledged Borrowings] - Refers to the amount of financing obtained by securities companies from banks through the method of pledging.
[Borrowings from the Central Bank] - Banks borrow temporary working capital loans, seasonal loans, annual loans, and special loans approved due to special needs from the central bank.
[Customer Deposits and Interbank Deposits] - Customer deposits absorbed by the bank or funds deposited in the bank by other financial institutions.
[Among them: Deposits from Other Banks and Financial Institutions] - Clearing funds deposited in the bank by other banks or financial institutions due to daily settlement transactions.
[Among them: Customer Deposits] - Various deposits absorbed by enterprises (banks) other than interbank deposits.
[Interbank Borrowed Funds] - Funds borrowed by financial enterprises from financial institutions.

[Trading Financial Liabilities] - The fair value of trading financial liabilities assumed by the enterprise. Financial liabilities that the enterprise directly designates to be measured at fair value and whose changes are recognized in the current profit or loss are also accounted for under this item. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Derivative Financial Liabilities] - The amount of derivative instruments, hedging instruments, and hedged items that are classified as derivative financial liabilities held by the enterprise.

[Notes Payable] - Notes payable issued by the company to offset payment for goods and other expenses that have not yet reached the payment due date, including bank acceptance bills and commercial acceptance bills. This item has been in use since 1991.
[Accounts Payable] - Amounts payable by the company to suppliers for the purchase of raw materials, goods, or the acceptance of labor services. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Advance Receipts] - Amounts received in advance by the company from purchasing units in accordance with the purchase contract. This item has been in use since 1990.

[Contract Liabilities] - Refers to the obligation of the enterprise to transfer goods to customers for which it has already received or is entitled to receive consideration from customers. Before transferring goods to customers, if the customer has already paid the contract consideration or the enterprise has obtained the unconditional right to receive the contract consideration, the enterprise should present the received or receivable amount as contract liabilities at the earlier of the actual payment date by the customer or the due payment date. This item has been in use since 2018.

[Proceeds from Sale and Repurchase of Financial Assets] - Funds raised by enterprises (financial institutions) through selling and then repurchasing bills, securities, loans, and other financial assets at a fixed price in accordance with the repurchase agreement. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Commissions and Fees Payable] - Commissions and fees that insurance enterprises should pay due to business transactions.

[Employee Remuneration Payable] - Various remunerations that enterprises should pay to employees in accordance with relevant regulations. Detailed accounting can be carried out for items such as "Salaries", "Employee Benefits", "Social Insurance Premiums", "Housing Provident Fund", "Union Funds", "Employee Education Funds", "Non-monetary Benefits", "Termination Benefits", and "Share-based Payments". This item has been in use since 2007.

[Taxes and Levies Payable] - Various taxes and levies that enterprises should pay calculated in accordance with tax laws and regulations, including value-added tax, consumption tax, business tax, income tax, resource tax, land appreciation tax, urban maintenance and construction tax, property tax, land use tax, vehicle and vessel use tax, education surcharge, mineral resources compensation fees, etc. Personal income tax withheld and paid on behalf of employees is also accounted for under this item. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Interest Payable] - Used to account for the interest accrued periodically by enterprises on long-term borrowings, bonds payable, and other long-term liabilities for which interest is paid periodically and the principal is repaid upon maturity. Note: This item has been in use since 2002 and is used by some enterprises.

[Dividends Payable] - Cash dividends that have been determined for distribution by the resolution of the company's board of directors or shareholders' meeting but have not yet been paid. This item has been in use since 1991.
[Claims Payable] - Claim amounts that insurance enterprises should pay but have not yet paid.
[Policy Dividends Payable] - Policy dividends that enterprises (insurance companies) should pay but have not yet paid to policyholders as agreed in the original insurance contracts.

[Policyholder Deposits and Investment Funds] - Deposits received by enterprises (insurance companies) from policyholders where the principal appreciation of the deposits is regarded as premium income, and investment funds received from policyholders for investment-oriented insurance business.
[Insurance Contract Reserves] - Insurance contract reserves include unearned premium reserves, outstanding claims reserves, life insurance reserves, and long-term health insurance reserves.
[Among them: Unearned Premium Reserves] - Unearned premium reserves refer to the reserves set aside by the insurer for non-life insurance liabilities that have not yet terminated.
[Among them: Outstanding Claims Reserves] - Outstanding claims reserves refer to the reserves set aside by the insurer for non-life insurance claims that have occurred but have not yet been settled.
[Among them: Life Insurance Reserves] - Life insurance reserves refer to the reserves set aside by the insurer for life insurance liabilities that have not yet terminated.

[Among them: Long-Term Health Insurance Reserves] - Long-term health insurance reserves refer to the reserves set aside by the insurer for long-term health insurance liabilities that have not yet terminated.

[Other Payables] - Various payable and temporarily received amounts of the enterprise other than notes payable, accounts payable, advance receipts, employee remuneration payable, interest payable, dividends payable, taxes and levies payable, long-term payables, etc. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Reinsurance Payables] - Amounts payable but not yet paid by enterprises (insurance companies) engaged in reinsurance business. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Agency Securities Trading Funds] - Funds received by enterprises (securities firms) from clients when acting on behalf of the clients to buy and sell negotiable securities such as stocks, bonds, and funds. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Agency Underwriting Securities Funds] - The underwriting funds payable to the securities issuers, which are formed when enterprises (financial institutions) accept the entrustment to underwrite securities through the methods of firm commitment underwriting or consignment underwriting. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Advance Premiums] - Premiums received by enterprises (insurance companies) that do not meet the criteria for premium income recognition yet.
[Non-Current Liabilities Due within One Year] - The book value of non-current liabilities that are due within one year. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Other Current Liabilities] - Current liabilities that cannot be classified into other specific current liability items.

[Deferred Income - Current Liabilities] - Deferred income refers to the income or gains that are yet to be recognized, or in other words, the temporarily unrecognized income. This item has been in use since 2015.
[Total Current Liabilities] - The total of all current liability items. This item has been in use since 1990.

[Long-Term Borrowings] - Various borrowings with a term of more than one year (excluding one year) that the company borrows from banks or other financial institutions. This item has been in use since 1990.

[Separate Account Liabilities] - Separate account liabilities recognized by enterprises (insurance companies) for the portion of investment-linked products that is not part of the risk protection and is accounted for separately.

[Bonds Payable] - The principal and interest of bonds issued by the enterprise to raise (long-term) funds. For convertible corporate bonds issued by the enterprise, the liability and equity components should be separated, and the liability component formed after separation is accounted for under this item.
[Lease Liabilities] - The present value of lease payments that have not been paid yet. This item has been in use since 2019.

[Long-Term Payables] - Various long-term payables of the company other than long-term borrowings and bonds payable, including the 价款 for the introduction of foreign equipment under the compensation trade method and the lease fees for fixed assets leased through financing leases. This item has been in use since 1991.

[Special Payables] - Payables formed when the company undertakes special construction tasks, such as payables for three specific science and technology expenses. Note: This item has been in use since 2000 and is a reserve item.

[Total Long-Term Liabilities] - The total of all long-term liability items. The calculation formula is: Total Long-Term Liabilities = Long-Term Borrowings + Separate Account Liabilities + Bonds Payable + Lease Liabilities + Long-Term Payables + Special Payables.

[Provisions] - Various contingent liabilities estimated by the company, such as estimated pending litigation expenses. Before 2007, it belonged to current liabilities, and after 2007, it belongs to non-current liabilities. Note: This item has been in use since 2000.
[Agency Business Liabilities] - Funds received from agency business where the company does not assume risks, including entrusted investment funds and entrusted loan funds.
[Deferred Tax Liabilities] - Income tax liabilities recognized by the enterprise arising from taxable temporary differences. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Other Non-Current Liabilities] - The total of non-current liabilities other than the above-mentioned non-current liabilities. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Deferred Income - Non-Current Liabilities] - Deferred income refers to the income or gains that are yet to be recognized, or in other words, the temporarily unrecognized income. This item has been in use since 2015.
[Total Non-Current Liabilities] - The total of all non-current liabilities. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Other Liabilities] - Other liabilities disclosed by financial institutions.
[Total Liabilities] - The total of all liability items. This item has been in use since 1990.

[Paid-In Capital (or Share Capital)] - The difference between the total amount of share capital invested by shareholders into the company according to the company's articles of association and the repaid investments.

[Other Equity Instruments] - Account for various financial instruments issued by the enterprise that are classified as equity instruments other than common shares. Detailed accounting should be carried out according to the types of financial instruments issued. This item has been in use since 2015.

[Among them: Preferred Shares] - Preferred shares are relative to common shares, mainly referring to the fact that in terms of the rights to profit distribution and residual property distribution, they have priority over common shares. This item has been in use since 2015.

[Among them: Perpetual Bonds] - Perpetual bonds mean that the borrower does not stipulate a maturity date, and the holder cannot demand repayment of the principal but can receive interest on a regular basis. This item has been in use since 2015.
[Among them: Others] - Other contents that cannot be classified into other equity instruments. This item has been in use since 2015.

[Capital Surplus] - The ending balance of the company's capital surplus. It includes share premium, statutory property revaluation increment, transfer of housing provident fund, the value of donated assets, investment reserve, etc. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Among them: Treasury Shares] - The amount of the company's own shares that have been acquired, transferred, or cancelled. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Surplus Reserve] - Reserve funds extracted from profits in accordance with relevant national regulations. It includes statutory surplus reserve, discretionary surplus reserve, and public welfare fund, which are extracted at a certain percentage of the post-tax profit after deducting the losses of previous years (if any). This item has been in use since 1991.
[General Risk Reserve] - General risk reserve that enterprises (financial institutions) extract from the net profit as required.
[Undistributed Profits] - Profits of the company that have not been distributed yet. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Foreign Currency Translation Differences] - The differences in currency conversion resulting from different functional currencies.

[Add: Unrecognized Investment Losses] - For long-term investment items accounted for using the equity method when preparing consolidated financial statements, when the owner's equity of the invested enterprise is negative, it represents the share of the negative owner's equity of the invested enterprise that the company undertakes. This item has been in use since 1997 and was discontinued in 2007. Losses are filled in with a "-" sign.

[Trading Risk Reserve] - Trading risk reserve that securities companies extract from the annual post-tax profit, which is used to make up for the losses in securities trading. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Special Reserve] - Special reserve is used to account for expenses with similar nature, such as safety production expenses and costs for maintaining simple reproduction, which are extracted by enterprises in high-risk industries as required. This item has been in use since 2000.

[Other Comprehensive Income] - The net amount of various gains and losses that enterprises do not recognize in profit or loss according to the accounting standards for enterprises, after deducting the impact of income tax. This item has been in use since 2015.

[Total Equity Attributable to the Owners of the Parent Company] - The equity attributable to the owners of the parent company in the consolidated financial statements. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Minority Interests] - The share of the owner's equity of the subsidiary that is owned by other investors except the parent company. Note: This item has been in use since 1991.
[Total Owners' Equity] - The total of all items of shareholders' equity. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Total Liabilities and Owners' Equity] - The total of all items of liabilities and shareholders' equity. This item has been in use since 1990.

[Total Operating Revenue] - The sum of all revenues during the enterprise's operation process. The calculation formula is: Total Operating Revenue = Operating Revenue + Net Interest Income + Earned Premiums + Net Fees and Commissions Income + Other Business Income.
[Operating Revenue] - Operating revenue recognized during the enterprise's operation process.
[Net Interest Income] - The difference between the interest income recognized by the enterprise and the interest expense incurred.

[Interest Income] - Interest income recognized by enterprises (financial institutions), including interest income from various loans issued (syndicated loans, trade financing, funds lent through discount and rediscount, agreed overdrafts, credit card overdrafts, relending, advances, etc.), fund transactions with other financial institutions (central bank, interbank, etc.), and interest income realized from financial assets purchased under resale agreements, etc.

[Interest Expense] - Interest expense incurred by enterprises (financial institutions), including interest expense from various deposits absorbed (corporate deposits, personal deposits, credit card deposits, special deposits, relending funds, etc.), fund transactions with other financial institutions (central bank, interbank, etc.), and interest expense generated from financial assets sold under repurchase agreements, etc.

[Earned Premiums] - It reflects the balance after subtracting the amounts of the "Reinsurance Premiums" and "Unearned Premium Reserves Withdrawn" items from the amount of the "Insurance Business Income" item.
[Insurance Business Income] - It reflects the original premium income and reinsurance premium income recognized by the enterprise from engaging in insurance business.
[Among them: Reinsurance Premium Income] - It reflects the income recognized by the enterprise from engaging in reinsurance business.
[Less: Reinsurance Premiums] - It reflects the premiums ceded by the enterprise from engaging in reinsurance business.
[Less: Unearned Premium Reserves Withdrawn] - Unearned premium reserves of non-life original insurance contracts and reinsurance contracts that are withdrawn by the enterprise (insurance company).
[Net Fees and Commissions Income] - The difference between the fees and commissions income recognized by the enterprise and the various fees and commissions expenses incurred.
[Among them: Net Income from Agency Securities Trading Business] - The difference between the income and expenses of the agency securities trading business of securities companies.
[Among them: Net Income from Securities Underwriting Business] - The difference between the income and expenses of the securities underwriting business of securities companies.
[Among them: Net Income from Entrusted Client Asset Management Business] - The difference between the income and expenses of the entrusted client asset management business of securities companies.

[Fees and Commissions Income] - Fees and commissions income recognized by the enterprise (financial institution), including fees and commissions obtained from agency services such as settlement business, consulting business, guarantee business, and custody business, as well as from handling entrusted loans and investment business.
[Fees and Commissions Expenses] - Various fees and commissions expenses incurred by the enterprise (financial institution) related to its business activities.
[Other Business Income] - Income recognized from other business operations of the enterprise.

[Total Operating Costs] - The sum of all costs during the enterprise's operation process. Before June 30, 2019, the calculation formula was: Total Operating Costs = Operating Cost + Surrender Value + Net Claims Expenses + Net Increase in Insurance Liability Reserves + Policyholder Dividends + Reinsurance Expenses - Less: Reinsurance Expenses Recovered + Taxes and Surcharges + Business and Management Fees + Insurance Business Fees and Commissions Expenses + Selling Expenses + Administrative Expenses + Financial Expenses + R&D Expenses + Other Operating Costs + Asset Impairment Losses + Credit Impairment Losses. After June 30, 2019 (including June 30, 2019), the calculation formula was: Total Operating Costs = Operating Cost + Surrender Value + Net Claims Expenses + Net Increase in Insurance Liability Reserves + Policyholder Dividends + Reinsurance Expenses - Less: Reinsurance Expenses Recovered + Taxes and Surcharges + Business and Management Fees + Insurance Business Fees and Commissions Expenses + Selling Expenses + Administrative Expenses + Financial Expenses + R&D Expenses + Other Operating Costs. The data on January 1, 2019, was based on the beginning-of-period data on December 31, 2019, so the calculation formula conforms to that after June 30, 2019.
[Operating Cost] - Operating cost recognized by the enterprise.
[Surrender Value] - The cash value of the policy that the enterprise (insurance company) should return to the policyholder when the original life insurance contract is terminated early as agreed.
[Net Claims Expenses] - It reflects the balance after subtracting the amount of the "Reinsurance Claims Expense Recovered" item from the amount of the "Claims Expenses" item.
[Claims Expenses] - Claim payments made by the enterprise (insurance company) for original insurance contracts and reinsurance contracts.
[Less: Reinsurance Claims Expense Recovered] - The claim costs recovered by the enterprise (ceding reinsurer) from the reinsurance acceptor.

[Net Increase in Insurance Liability Reserves] - It reflects the balance after subtracting the amount of the "Reinsurance Insurance Liability Reserves Recovered" item from the amount of the "Increase in Insurance Liability Reserves" item.

[Increase in Insurance Liability Reserves] - It reflects the insurance liability reserves withdrawn by the enterprise, including outstanding claims reserves, life insurance reserves, and long-term health insurance reserves.

[Less: Reinsurance Insurance Liability Reserves Recovered] - The insurance liability reserves that the enterprise (ceding reinsurer) should recover from the reinsurance acceptor when engaging in reinsurance business.
[Policyholder Dividends] - Dividends paid by the enterprise (insurance company) to the policyholders as agreed in the original insurance contracts.
[Reinsurance Expenses] - Reinsurance expenses paid by the enterprise (reinsurance acceptor) to the ceding reinsurer.

[Taxes and Surcharges] - Relevant taxes and fees such as business tax, consumption tax, urban maintenance and construction tax, resource tax, and education surcharge incurred in the enterprise's business activities. After the new accounting standards in 2007, the item "Main Business Taxes and Surcharges" was cancelled, and "Business Taxes and Surcharges" was used instead. According to the provisions of Document CaiKuai [2016] No. 22, after the full implementation of the "Replacement of Business Tax with Value-Added Tax", the name of the "Business Taxes and Surcharges" account was adjusted to the "Taxes and Surcharges" account.

[Business and Management Fees] - Various expenses incurred by the enterprise (financial institution) in the process of business operation and management, including electronic equipment operation fees, security prevention fees, property management fees, etc.
[Less: Reinsurance Expenses Recovered] - It reflects the reinsurance expenses recovered by the enterprise from the reinsurance acceptor when engaging in reinsurance ceding business.
[Insurance Business Fees and Commissions Expenses] - It reflects the fees and commissions expenses incurred by the enterprise when engaging in insurance business.

[Selling Expenses] - Expenses incurred during the process of the company's goods sales, including transportation fees, loading and unloading fees, packaging fees, insurance fees, exhibition fees, and advertising fees.

[Administrative Expenses] - Administrative expenses incurred by the enterprise for organizing and managing its production and operation. After the new accounting standards in 2007, the asset impairment losses originally included in administrative expenses were accounted for in the "Asset Impairment Losses" account.
[R&D Expenses] - R&D expenses refer to the expenditures on research and development costs. This item has been in use since 2018.

[Financial Expenses] - Expenses incurred by the company for raising funds required for production and operation, including interest expenses (less interest income), exchange losses (less exchange gains), and related fees.
[Among them: Interest Expenses (Financial Expenses)] - The funds occupancy fees paid by the enterprise for debt financing in production and operation. This item has been in use since 2018.

[Among them: Interest Income (Financial Expenses)] - Income obtained by the enterprise from providing funds to others for use that does not constitute equity investment, or from others' occupancy of the enterprise's funds, including income such as deposit interest, loan interest, bond interest, and arrears interest. This item has been in use since 2018.

[Other Income] - It is used to account for government subsidies related to the enterprise's daily activities that are not suitable to be recognized as revenue or to offset cost expenses. This item has been in use since 2017.

[Investment Income] - Income obtained by the company from external investments in various ways. After the new accounting standards in 2007, the asset impairment losses originally included in investment income were accounted for in the "Asset Impairment Losses" account. This item has been in use since 1991.
[Among them: Investment Income from Associates and Joint Ventures] - The investment income of the company from associates and joint ventures in the current period.

[Among them: Gains or Losses on Derecognition of Financial Assets Measured at Amortized Cost] - It reflects the gains or losses generated by the enterprise due to the derecognition of financial assets measured at amortized cost caused by situations such as transfer. This item has been in use since 2019.
[Exchange Gains] - Exchange gains generated by the enterprise (financial institution) from foreign currency transactions due to exchange rate fluctuations.

[Net Gains on Hedging] - It reflects the amount transferred to current profit or loss from the cumulative fair value changes of hedged items under net exposure hedging or the amount transferred from cash flow hedge reserves to current profit or loss. This item has been in use since 2019.

[Gains or Losses from Changes in Fair Value] - Gains or losses that should be included in current profit or loss formed by the changes in fair value of the enterprise's trading financial assets, trading financial liabilities, investment property measured at fair value, derivative instruments, hedging business, etc.
[Asset Impairment Losses] - Losses formed by the enterprise when making provisions for impairment of various assets.

[Credit Impairment Losses] - Losses suffered by the enterprise due to reasons such as the purchaser's refusal to pay, bankruptcy, or death, resulting in uncollectible amounts. This item has been in use since 2019.

[Gains or Losses on Disposal of Assets] - It reflects the disposal gains or losses recognized when the enterprise sells non-current assets (excluding financial instruments, long-term equity investments, and investment property) or disposal groups classified as held for sale, as well as the disposal gains or losses generated from the disposal of fixed assets, construction in progress, productive biological assets, and intangible assets that are not classified as held for sale. Gains or losses from the disposal of non-current assets in debt restructuring and gains or losses from non-monetary asset exchanges are also included in this item. This item has been in use since 2017.
[Other Operating Costs] - Costs incurred in other business operations of the enterprise.

[Other Operating Profits] - Profits obtained from other sales or other business activities of the company except for the main business, after deducting other operating costs, expenses, and taxes. This item was in use from 1990 to 2007.

[Operating Profit] - Profit related to business operations. Before June 30, 2019, the calculation formula was: operating profit=total operating revenue - total operating costs+fair value change income+investment income+exchange rate income+other business profits+other income+net exposure hedging income+asset disposal income. The calculation formula after June 30, 2019 is: operating profit=total operating revenue - total operating costs+fair value change income+investment income+exchange rate income+other business profits+other income+net exposure hedging income+asset disposal income+asset impairment loss+credit impairment loss. Among them, the data for January 1, 2019 is extracted from the initial data of December 31, 2019, so the calculation formula conforms to the calculation formula after June 30, 2019.

[Add: Non-Operating Income] - This account is used to record various non-operating incomes of the enterprise, mainly including gains from the disposal of non-current assets, gains from non-monetary asset exchanges, gains from debt restructuring, government subsidies, inventory profits, and donation gains, etc. This item has been in use since 1990.
[Among them: Gains from the Disposal of Non-Current Assets] - Including gains from the disposal of fixed assets and gains from the sale of intangible assets. This item has been in use since 2015.

[Less: Non-Operating Expenses] - Various non-operating expenses incurred by the enterprise, including losses from the disposal of non-current assets, losses from non-monetary asset exchanges, losses from debt restructuring, public welfare donation expenditures, extraordinary losses, and inventory shortages losses, etc. Since 2007, according to the new accounting standards, the asset impairment losses originally included in non-operating expenses are accounted for in the "Asset Impairment Losses" account. This item has been in use since 1990.

[Among them: Net Profits or Losses from the Disposal of Non-Current Assets] - The total net profits or losses generated from the disposal of non-current assets within the year. This item has been in use since 2007. The calculation formula is: Net Profits or Losses from the Disposal of Non-Current Assets = Gains from the Disposal of Non-Current Assets - Losses from the Disposal of Non-Current Assets.
[Among them: Losses from the Disposal of Non-Current Assets] - Including losses from the disposal of fixed assets and losses from the sale of intangible assets. This item has been in use since 2015.

[Total Profit] - The total profit realized by the company. This item has been in use since 1990. The calculation formula is: Total Profit = Operating Profit + Non-Operating Income - Non-Operating Expenses.
[Less: Income Tax Expense] - The income tax expense recognized by the enterprise that should be deducted from the current total profit.

[Unrecognized Investment Losses] - In the case of accounting for long-term investment projects using the equity method, when preparing consolidated financial statements, if the owner's equity of the invested enterprise is negative, the share of the negative owner's equity that the company should bear. This item was in use from 1998 to 2007.
[Other Items Affecting Net Profit] - Other items that have an impact on net profit.
[Net Profit] - The net profit achieved by the company. Note: This item has been in use since 1990, and some companies did not have this item before 1994.

[Net Profit Attributable to Owners of the Parent Company] - The net profit in the consolidated financial statements that is attributable to the owners of the parent company. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Profit Attributable to Holders of Other Equity Instruments of the Parent Company] - The net profit generated from the issuance of other equity instruments such as cumulative preferred shares by subsidiaries of the parent company, which is attributable to the holders of these instruments. This item has been in use since 2018.

[Minority Interests in Profit or Loss] - The profit or loss that should be enjoyed or shared by minority shareholders, calculated based on the proportion of the company's equity held by minority shareholders in the annual profit and loss of the subsidiary. This item has been in use since 1991.

[Basic Earnings per Share] - An enterprise should calculate the basic earnings per share by dividing the current period's net profit attributable to common shareholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Diluted Earnings per Share] - If an enterprise has dilutive potential common shares, it should adjust the current period's net profit attributable to common shareholders and the weighted average number of common shares outstanding respectively, and calculate the diluted earnings per share based on the adjusted figures. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Other Comprehensive Income (Loss)] - The net amount of various gains and losses that are not recognized in profit or loss as stipulated by the accounting standards for enterprises, after deducting the impact of income tax. This item has been in use since 2009.

[Total Comprehensive Income] - Comprehensive income refers to all kinds of income excluding the capital contributions from owners and various amounts collected on behalf of third parties or customers. This item has been in use since 2009.

[Comprehensive Income Attributable to Owners of the Parent Company] - The portion of the total comprehensive income that is attributable to the owners of the parent company. This item has been in use since 2009.

[Total Comprehensive Income Attributable to Holders of Other Equity Instruments of the Parent Company] - The portion of the total comprehensive income that is attributable to the holders of other equity instruments of the parent company.

[Comprehensive Income Attributable to Minority Shareholders] - The profit distribution occupied by minority shareholders in the comprehensive profit and loss according to their equity proportion. This item has been in use since 2009.

[Cash Received from the Sale of Goods and the Provision of Services] - The cash actually received by the company from the sale of goods (including the sale of goods, products, and materials, the same below) and the provision of services, including the cash received in the current period from the sale of goods and the provision of services, the cash received in the current period from the sale of goods and the provision of services in the previous period, and the advances received in the current period, minus the cash paid for the return of goods sold in the current period and the return of goods sold in the previous period but returned in the current period.

[Net Increase in Customer Deposits and Interbank Deposits] - The net increase in various deposits absorbed in the current period from domestic and foreign financial institutions and other deposits excluding non-interbank deposits. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Decrease in Deposits with the Central Bank and Interbank Deposits] - The net decrease in the amounts deposited with the central bank and domestic and foreign financial institutions in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Net Increase in Borrowings from the Central Bank] - The net increase in the amounts borrowed from the central bank in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Increase in Funds Borrowed from Other Financial Institutions] - The net amount of cash obtained from borrowing funds from domestic and foreign financial institutions in the current period, minus the cash paid for lending funds to domestic and foreign financial institutions. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Cash Received from Premiums of Original Insurance Contracts] - It reflects the cash received by the insurance company from the premiums of original insurance contracts in the current period. It includes the original insurance premium income received in the current period, the previous period's receivable original insurance premiums received in the current period, the advance original insurance premiums received in the current period, and the original insurance premiums collected on behalf of other enterprises in the current period, minus the cash paid for the refund of premiums due to the early termination of insurance contracts in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Cash Received from Reinsurance Business] - The actual amount received from reinsurers or reinsurance acceptors in the current period for reinsurance business. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Increase in Policyholder Deposits and Investment Funds] - The actual increase in the deposits received from policyholders in the current period, where the rent interest is recognized as premium income, and the investment principal of investment-type insurance business. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Increase in Cash from the Disposal of Trading Financial Assets] - The net increase in cash obtained by securities companies from the self-trading of trading financial assets in the current period. This item has been used in consolidated financial statements since the new accounting standards in 2007. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Cash Received from Interest, Fees, and Commissions] - The amount of interest, fees, and commissions received in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Increase in Borrowed Funds] - The net increase in the cash obtained from borrowing funds from domestic and foreign financial institutions in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Increase in Funds from Repurchase Transactions] - The net amount of cash raised by selling financial assets such as bills, securities, and loans under repurchase agreements in the current period, minus the cash paid for purchasing and then reselling these financial assets at a fixed price to the buyer as agreed in the resale agreement. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Net Decrease in Lent Funds] - The net decrease in the amounts lent to domestic and foreign financial institutions in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Decrease in Payments for Financial Assets Purchased under Resale Agreements] - The net decrease in the amounts paid by the enterprise for purchasing and then reselling financial assets at a fixed price as agreed in the resale agreement in the current period.

[Tax Refunds Received] - It reflects various tax refunds received by the enterprise, such as value-added tax refunds, business tax refunds, income tax refunds, consumption tax refunds, customs duty refunds, and education surcharge refunds.

[Other Cash Received Related to Operating Activities] - Other cash received by the company related to operating activities, excluding the above items, such as cash income from donations, fines, and compensation for losses of current assets by individuals. If there are items with relatively large amounts among the other cash received related to operating activities, they should be reflected as separate items.
[Subtotal of Cash Inflows from Operating Activities] - The subtotal of cash inflows from operating activities.

[Cash Paid for the Purchase of Goods and the Acceptance of Services] - The cash actually paid by the company for the purchase of goods and the acceptance of services, including the cash paid in the current period for the purchase of goods and the acceptance of services, the unpaid amounts for the purchase of goods and the acceptance of services in the previous period paid in the current period, the advance payments made in the current period, and the value-added tax paid for the purchase of goods or the acceptance of services provided by small-scale taxpayers. The cash received from the return of purchased goods in the current period (excluding the value-added tax refunded for the return of goods purchased from general taxpayers) should be deducted from this item.

[Net Increase in Customer Loans and Advances] - The net increase in various customer loans issued in the current period, as well as the amounts for handling commercial bill discounting, rediscounting, and other business operations such as lending and borrowing funds. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Net Decrease in Borrowings from the Central Bank] - The net decrease in the amounts borrowed from the central bank in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Increase in Deposits with the Central Bank and Interbank Deposits] - The net increase in the amounts deposited with the central bank and domestic and foreign financial institutions in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Cash Paid for Claim Payments of Original Insurance Contracts] - It reflects the cash actually paid by the insurance company for the claim payments of original insurance contracts in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Cash Paid for Interest, Fees, and Commissions] - The cash actually paid for interest, fees, and commissions outflows in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Net Cash Paid for Reinsurance Business] - The actual amount paid to reinsurers or reinsurance acceptors for reinsurance business in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Decrease in Policyholder Deposits and Investment Funds] - The actual decrease in the deposits received from policyholders, where the rent interest is recognized as premium income, and the investment principal of investment-type insurance business in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.
[Net Increase in Lent Funds] - The net increase in the amounts lent to domestic and foreign financial institutions in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Increase in Payments for Financial Assets Purchased under Resale Agreements] - The net increase in the amounts paid by the enterprise for purchasing and then reselling financial assets at a fixed price as agreed in the resale agreement in the current period.

[Net Decrease in Borrowed Funds] - The net decrease in the cash obtained from borrowing funds from domestic and foreign financial institutions in the current period. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Net Decrease in Funds Raised from Selling Financial Assets under Repurchase Agreements] - The net decrease in the funds raised by the enterprise (financial institution) from selling financial assets such as bills, securities, and loans under repurchase agreements in the current period.

[Cash Paid for Policyholder Dividends] - Cash actually paid to policyholders by enterprises (insurance companies) as stipulated in the original insurance contracts. This item has been in use since 2007.

[Cash Paid to Employees and on Behalf of Employees] - Cash actually paid to employees and for employees by the company, including salaries, bonuses, various allowances and subsidies actually paid to employees in the current period, as well as expenses for endowment insurance, unemployment insurance, supplementary endowment insurance, housing provident fund, housing hardship subsidies for employees, and expenses for retired personnel. It does not include the salaries paid to personnel working on construction in progress projects.

[Various Taxes and Fees Paid] - Various taxes and fees incurred and paid by the enterprise in the current period, taxes and fees paid in the current period that were incurred in previous periods, and prepaid taxes and fees such as education surcharge, mineral resources compensation fees, stamp duty, property tax, land appreciation tax, vehicle and vessel use tax, and prepaid business tax. Excluded are taxes and fees included in the value of fixed assets, actual paid cultivated land occupation tax, and value-added tax and income tax refunded in the current period.

[Other Cash Payments Related to Operating Activities] - Other cash payments related to operating activities made by the company, excluding the above items, such as cash donations, fines, travel expenses, cash expenditures for business entertainment, insurance premiums, power expenses, sewage disposal fees, pension contributions, maintenance and repair costs, research and development expenses, rental expenses, and other expenses. If there are items with relatively large amounts among other cash payments related to operating activities, they should be separately listed for reflection.
[Subtotal of Cash Outflows from Operating Activities] - Subtotal of cash outflows from operating activities.
[Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities] - The difference between cash inflows and cash outflows generated from operating activities.

[Cash Received from the Recovery of Investments] - It reflects the cash received by the enterprise from selling, transferring, or recovering upon maturity of trading assets, held-to-maturity investments, available-for-sale financial assets, long-term equity investments, and investment real estate, excluding cash equivalents. It does not include the interest recovered from debt investments, recovered non-cash assets, interest recovered from debt investments, and the net cash received from the disposal of subsidiaries and other business units.

[Cash Received from Investment Income] - Cash dividends and interest obtained by the enterprise from equity investments and debt investments, as well as cash received from the distribution of profits from subsidiaries, associated enterprises, and joint ventures. Note: This item is a combination of the items "Cash Received from Dividends or Profits" and "Cash Received from Bond Interest Income" in the years before 2000.

[Net Cash Received from the Disposal of Fixed Assets, Intangible Assets, and Other Long-Term Assets] - It reflects the net amount of cash obtained by the enterprise from selling fixed assets, intangible assets, and other long-term assets, after deducting the relevant expenses paid for the disposal of these assets. If the net cash received from the disposal of fixed assets, intangible assets, and other long-term assets is negative, it should be reflected in the item "Other Cash Payments Related to Investing Activities".
[Net Cash Received from Disposal of Subsidiaries and Other Business Units] - Net cash received from disposing of subsidiaries and other business units during the current period.

[Cash Received Related to Other Investing Activities] - Cash received related to other investing activities, apart from the items listed above. If there are significant amounts, they should be separately listed.
[Subtotal of Cash Inflows from Investing Activities] - null

[Cash Paid for Acquisition of Fixed Assets, Intangible Assets, and Other Long-Term Assets] - Cash paid for acquiring and constructing fixed assets, intangible assets, and other long-term assets. It excludes the capitalized borrowing costs for acquiring fixed assets and the lease payments for financing leases. The borrowing costs and lease payments for financing leases are separately reflected in the cash flow from financing activities. When a company acquires fixed assets by installment payment, the cash paid for the initial payment is regarded as the cash outflow of investing activities, and the cash paid in subsequent periods is regarded as the cash outflow of financing activities.

[Cash Paid for Investments] - Cash paid for equity and debt investments, including the cash paid for acquiring trading financial assets, held-to-maturity investments, available-for-sale financial assets (excluding cash equivalents), as well as related additional fees such as commissions and service charges.
[Net Increase in Pledged Loans] - Net increase in policyholder pledged loans issued during the current period. Since 2007, it has been in use.
[Net Cash Paid for Acquisition of Subsidiaries and Other Business Units] - Net cash paid for purchasing subsidiaries and other business units during the current period.（原翻译 “购买和处置” 不准确，这里强调的是购买支付的现金）

[Cash Paid Related to Other Investing Activities] - Cash paid related to other investing activities, apart from the items listed above. If there are significant amounts, they should be separately listed.
[Subtotal of Cash Outflows from Investing Activities] - null
[Net Cash Flow from Investing Activities] - The difference between cash inflows and cash outflows from investing activities.

[Cash Received from Equity Financing] - Net cash received from raising funds through issuing shares, bonds, and other financing methods. It excludes audit, consulting, and other fees directly paid by the enterprise for raising funds through such means.
[Cash Received from Equity Investments] - Net cash received from raising funds by issuing shares, which is the net amount after deducting issuance fees such as commissions from the issuing revenue.
[Of Which: Cash Received from Minority Shareholders' Investments in Subsidiaries] - Net cash received from minority shareholders' investments in subsidiaries in the consolidated financial statements.
[Cash Received from Issuing Bonds] - Cash received from raising funds by issuing bonds.
[Cash Received from Borrowings] - Funds borrowed by the company from banks or other financial institutions.

[Cash Received Related to Other Financing Activities] - Cash received related to other financing activities, apart from the items listed above. If there are significant amounts, they should be separately listed.
[Subtotal of Cash Inflows from Financing Activities] - null

[Cash Paid for Repaying Debts] - Cash paid for repaying the principal of debts, including the principal of borrowings from banks or other financial institutions and bond principal repayments. The interest on borrowings and bonds repaid by the company is not included in this item and is reflected in the item "Cash Paid for Paying Interest".

[Cash Paid for Distributing Dividends, Profits, or Paying Interest] - Cash actually paid for distributing cash dividends, paying profits to other investment entities, or paying interest on borrowings and bonds.
[Of Which: Dividends and Profits Paid to Minority Shareholders] - Dividends and profits paid to minority shareholders by subsidiaries in the consolidated financial statements.

[Cash Paid Related to Other Financing Activities] - Cash paid related to other financing activities, apart from the items listed above. If there are significant amounts, they should be separately listed.
[Subtotal of Cash Outflows from Financing Activities] - null
[Net Cash Flow from Financing Activities] - The difference between cash inflows and cash outflows from financing activities.

[Effect of Exchange Rate Changes on Cash and Cash Equivalents] - The difference between the amount of foreign currency cash flows converted into RMB at the exchange rate on the date of the cash flow or the average exchange rate and the amount of net foreign currency cash converted into RMB at the exchange rate at the end of the period.
[Other Effects on Cash] - Other accounts that affect cash.
[Net Increase in Cash and Cash Equivalents] - Net increase in cash and cash equivalents during the accounting period.
[Cash and Cash Equivalents at Beginning of Period] - Balance of cash and cash equivalents at the beginning of the period. Since 2007, it has been in use.
[Cash and Cash Equivalents at End of Period] - Balance of cash and cash equivalents at the end of the period. Since 2007, it has been in use.
[Net Profit] - Net profit realized by the enterprise during the current period.

[Credit Impairment Losses] - Losses incurred by the enterprise due to reasons such as the purchaser's refusal to pay, bankruptcy, or death, resulting in uncollectible receivables. Since 2019, it has been in use.

[Unrecognized Investment Losses] - In the case of accounting for long-term investments using the equity method, when preparing consolidated financial statements, if the owner's equity of the investee is negative, the share of the negative owner's equity that the company should bear. It was used from 1998 to 2007.
[Asset Impairment Provision] - Asset impairment provisions recognized by the enterprise during the current period.

[Depreciation of Fixed Assets, Depletion of Oil and Gas Assets, and Depreciation of Productive Biological Assets] - Depreciation of fixed assets, depletion of oil and gas assets, and depreciation of productive biological assets recognized by the enterprise during the current period. Since 2007, it has been in use.
[Amortization of Intangible Assets] - Value of intangible assets amortized and charged to cost expenses during the current period.
[Amortization of Long-Term Deferred Expenses] - Long-term deferred expenses amortized and charged to cost expenses during the current period.

[Loss on Disposal of Fixed Assets, Intangible Assets, and Other Long-Term Assets] - Net loss (if it is a gain, fill it with a "-" sign) from disposing of fixed assets, intangible assets, and other long-term assets during the current period.
[Loss from Scrapping Fixed Assets] - Net loss (if it is a gain, fill it with a "-" sign) after inventory shortages (minus inventory surpluses) of fixed assets during the current period.

[Loss from Changes in Fair Value] - Gains or losses from changes in the fair value of financial assets, financial liabilities, and investment property measured at fair value. Since 2007, it has been in use.

[Financial Expenses (if it is income, fill it with a "-" sign)] - Financial expenses incurred by the enterprise during the current period that should be attributed to investment or financing activities.
[Investment Loss (if it is a gain, fill it with a "-" sign)] - Net investment loss (calculated as losses minus gains) incurred by the enterprise during the current period.

[Decrease in Deferred Tax Assets (if it is an increase, fill it with a "-" sign)] - The difference between the beginning and ending balances of the "Deferred Tax Assets" item on the balance sheet. Since 2007, it has been in use.

[Increase in Deferred Tax Liabilities (if it is a decrease, fill it with a "-" sign)] - The difference between the beginning and ending balances of the "Deferred Tax Liabilities" item on the balance sheet. Since 2007, it has been in use.
[Decrease in Inventory (if it is an increase, fill it with a "-" sign)] - The decrease (minus the increase) in inventory during the current period.

[Decrease in Operating Receivables (if it is an increase, fill it with a "-" sign)] - The decrease (minus the increase) in operating receivables during the current period, including accounts receivable, notes receivable, the part of other receivables related to operating activities, and value-added tax output tax receivables.

[Increase in Operating Payables (if it is a decrease, fill it with a "-" sign)] - The increase (minus the decrease) in operating payables during the current period, including accounts payable, notes payable, welfare payables, taxes payable, the part of other payables related to operating activities, and value-added tax input tax payables.
[Other] - Other items that need to be adjusted.
[Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities] - The net cash flow generated from operating activities during the current period.
[Debt to Capital Conversion] - The amount of debt converted to capital during the current period.
[Convertible Corporate Bonds Due within One Year] - The principal and interest of convertible corporate bonds that mature within one year.

If the denominator is not disclosed, zero, or less than zero, or the numerator is less than zero, the result is NULL. Average balance of accounts receivable = (Ending balance of accounts receivable + Beginning balance of accounts receivable) / 2.

[Accounts Receivable Turnover Rate C] - Calculation formula: Operating income / Average balance of accounts receivable. If the denominator is not disclosed, zero, or less than zero, or the numerator is less than zero, the result is NULL. Average balance of accounts receivable = (Ending balance of accounts receivable + Ending balance of accounts receivable from the previous year) / 2.

[Accounts Receivable Turnover Rate D] - Calculation formula: Adjustment factor × (Operating income) / Average net balance of accounts receivable. Average net balance of accounts receivable = (Ending net balance of accounts receivable + Ending net balance of accounts receivable from the previous year) / 2. The adjustment factor is related to the accounting period of (Operating income, an item in the income statement) (i.e., the difference in months between the start date and the end date); specifically, it is 12 / (interval months). For example, for the first quarter: 12 / 3; for the first 6 months: 12 / 6; for January - September: 12 / 9, for the whole year: 1; the same applies below. If the denominator is not disclosed, zero, or less than zero, or the numerator is less than zero, the result is NULL.

(Operating income) TTM refers to the cumulative operating income of the listed company over the past 12 months. For any account A, A item TTM = A item current period value + A item annual report value from the previous year - A item data from the same period of the previous year. If the current period data is annual report data, then A item TTM = A item current period value. If the denominator is not disclosed, zero, or less than zero, or the numerator is less than zero, the result is NULL.

[Return on Assets (ROA) A] - Calculation formula: (Total profit + Financial expenses) / Total assets. If the denominator is not disclosed or is zero, the result is represented as NULL.

[Return on Assets (ROA) B] - Calculation formula: (Total profit + Financial expenses) / Average total assets. If the denominator is not disclosed or is zero, the result is represented as NULL. Average total assets = (Ending balance of total assets + Beginning balance of total assets) / 2.

[Return on Assets (ROA) C] - Calculation formula: (Total profit + Financial expenses) / Average total assets. If the denominator is not disclosed or is zero, the result is represented as NULL. [Return on Assets (ROA) TTM] - Calculation formula: (Total profit TTM + Financial expenses TTM) / Average total assets. [Return on Assets (ROA) A - Net Profit Basis] - Calculation formula: Net profit / Total assets balance. If the denominator is not disclosed or is zero, the result is represented as NULL.

[Return on Assets (ROA) B - Net Profit Basis] - Calculation formula: Net profit / Average total assets balance. If the denominator is not disclosed or is zero, the result is represented as NULL. [Return on Assets (ROA) C - Net Profit Basis] - Calculation formula: Net profit / Average total assets balance. If the denominator is not disclosed or is zero, the result is represented as NULL. [Return on Assets (ROA) TTM - Net Profit Basis] - Calculation formula: (Net profit TTM) / Average total assets balance.
